overview: Two modes of speciation, differing in whether a physical geographic barrier is involved in separating populations.
genZNote: Allopatric: new species form because a mountain (or ocean) got in the way. Sympatric: new species form even while living in the very same area.

aspects.label: Geographic Separation Required?
aspects.valueA: Yes — populations are physically separated by a geographic barrier (mountain, river, ocean).
aspects.valueB: No — new species arise within the same geographic area, without physical separation.

aspects.label: Typical Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Populations accumulate genetic differences independently until they can no longer interbreed.
aspects.valueB: Reproductive isolation arises through other means, such as polyploidy, habitat specialisation, or behavioural differences.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Darwin's finches diverging on separate Galapagos islands.
aspects.valueB: Polyploid plant species arising instantly within the same population as their parent species.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Sympatric speciation via instant polyploidy is common in plants, since a doubled chromosome number can immediately prevent successful interbreeding with the parent population.
overlay.memoryTrick: Allopatric = 'other homeland' — different places. Sympatric = 'same homeland' — same place.
overlay.commonMisconception: Sympatric speciation is not just a theoretical idea — polyploidy-driven sympatric speciation in plants is well-documented and relatively common.
